title: Installing Plugins
summary: Chapter 2, Installing Plugins, explains why Vim users want plugins and how Vim 8's native packages feature removes the need for a third-party plugin manager. It defines the script/plugin/package hierarchy, shows that installing a plugin means adding it to the 'runtimepath', and demonstrates installing plugins under $VIMCONFIG/pack/{package}/start for automatic loading or under opt for on-demand loading with :packadd, plus indexing their documentation with :helptags. The chapter then covers updating plugins with git pull, migrating from Pathogen, and managing plugins with minpac (minpac#add(), minpac#update(), minpac#clean()) including user-defined commands such as :PackUpdate and :PackClean.

Let’s install the Scriptease plugin[16] this way. This plugin provides extra functionality that is useful when developing Vim script files.

concepts.name: Registering plugins with minpac#add()
concepts.evidence: To register plugins with your minpac package, you would call the minpac#add() function. As its first argument, this function takes a string made up of two parts separated with a slash ( / ): the plugin author’s GitHub username, followed by the name of the plugin. This function can also take an optional second argument, which is a dictionary of configuration options.
